svg.title: RIEMANN R7 — The Tate-Shafarevich bound: every statement of the chapter, and what each one rests on
svg.desc: The blueprint's chapter 7 in one poster: its 35 statements as cards, each with the Lean declaration it stands for, the statement in words, how its proof goes, and what it uses and is used by. Read it from the foot up: the chapter's theorem, thm-sha-bound, is at the bottom, and every card stands above the cards whose proofs use it. An arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A; a dashed arrow says that the proof of B names A without listing it as a use. The statements that head a section or a group of results have full cards; the others are drawn shorter. The chapter's own introduction: This chapter proves thm-sha-bound and shows where the rest of the proof uses it. For a primitive Dirichlet character ψ the ψ-fields E are abelian fields in a 2-power cyclotomic tower (def-sha-bound). The theorem says that the Tate–Shafarevich groups Ш^1_l(E, e) of the Tate twists Q_l/Z_l(-e), 0 < e < t = ⌊ x^(401)⌋, are finite, and that the sum of their lengths, weighted by log l, is at most e^(x^ε/2). The families of definite unitary groups (chap-families) carry an error term that these lengths control, and the bound keeps that term small. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.

A → B: the proof of B uses A (the arrow takes A's colour)
A ⇢ B: the proof of B names A without listing it as a use (dashed)
Title and pill. The title is the blueprint's; the pill gives the kind and the provenance: new in Alpöge's proof, modified from a published result, or published as it stands.

The Lean panel is the signature of the first declaration the blueprint lists for the statement, as lean-facts.json records it, wrapped and cut at nine lines (four on a short card). The footer gives its file and
line in the mirror and the other declarations.
The line in italics is the blueprint's statement, and the bullets are its proof, paragraph by paragraph, abridged where marked with …; links appear as ids and maths is rewritten in plain Unicode.
Stated with, Proof uses and Used by are the blueprint's edges. A proof use outside the chapter is counted, not drawn. Rows: a card's row is one above the highest card whose proof uses it, or higher
where that makes room; a card sits under the cards that use it where it can. A short card shows four lines of the signature and one paragraph of the proof.

text.tspan: 2 · The chapter, from its leaves down to its theorem

svg.text: 10 rows. Section by section the chapter runs: 1. Second cohomology of Tate twists (2); 2. Selmer groups from Kato's Euler system (3); 3. Kato's explicit reciprocity law (5); 4. Automorphy of symplectic lifts (5); 5. The error term of the families (8); 6. Congruence modules and Selmer groups (2); 7. Local lifting theorems for crystalline lattices (8). The cards keep that order within a row where the arrows allow.

text.tspan: Congruence bound at the auxiliary primes

svg.text: theorem main_alt_alt : Hypotheses₂ → ∃ (C : ℝ) (CT : ℕ), 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀
There are constants C ≥ 0 and C_T such that every member satisfying the Galois conditions
and the character conditions at g_0, g_1 has the two following properties. At each local datum
at a twisted place with l ≠ g_0, g_1 there is a Hecke-equivariant endomorphism acting by a
fixed nonzero integer on the good eigensystems and by 0 on the others.
The endomorphism comes from [global Artin reciprocity](@thm-artin-reciprocity). The bound

on inertia at l, and W : G_ℚ → GL_2(ℚ̄_l) a representation such that: det W = θ, W has
level N|D_K| and is ordinary at l with weights (e, -e), upper triangular on a decomposition
Sphericity and ordinary newforms. First, W is spherical at l: every cuspidal representation of
GL_2(A_ℚ) attached to a twist of W by a character of finite order is unramified at l when the
Kolyvagin's argument. So W and its twist by det W come from l-ordinary newforms of level
prime to l, and thm-kato-euler-system-ordinary gives each an Euler system whose
bottom class is not in the ordinary local condition at l. …

Σ)log lsum_(e=1)^(t-1)len Ш^1_l(E, e) ≤ e^(x^ε/2) for every finite set of primes Σ.

text.tspan: 3 · The argument in the chapter's own words, section by section

svg.text: The first paragraph of each section's introduction in the blueprint, in the chapter's order, with the statements each section holds. Abridged where marked with ….
Besides Selmer groups, the reduction in the proof of thm-sha-bound leaves the groups H^2
(G_(L,S), Z_l(e+1) ) of Tate twists, whose order lem-h2-tate-twists-bound bounds.
The proof builds classes in the homology of GL_n(mathcal O_L) from cyclic subgroups and
detects them by reduction at primes of degree one, a form of Soulé's comparison of this
homology with Galois cohomology. A rank bound of Borel type (
thm-borel-type-rank-bound) limits how many such classes there are.

text.tspan: 2. Selmer groups from Kato's Euler system

svg.text: In the first case of the proof of thm-sha-bound, l outside the bad set and l - 1 nmid 2e,
the Selmer groups are those of 2-dimensional representations W of G_ℚ, ordinary at l.
thm-kato-selmer-vanishing shows that their Bloch–Kato Selmer groups vanish, by
Kolyvagin's argument applied to Kato's Euler system. thm-kato-euler-system-ordinary
builds that Euler system for l-ordinary newforms from integral norm-compatible zeta classes (
thm-kato-zeta-integral); the reciprocity law of sec-sha-reciprocity shows that its
bottom class is not ordinary at l.
Kato's explicit reciprocity law (thm-kato-explicit-reciprocity) computes the image at l
of the zeta classes of thm-kato-zeta-integral as the value of a Hecke-equivariant
functional on Eisenstein series; the Euler system of thm-kato-euler-system-ordinary
needs it. The proof reduces to zeta classes of fixed exponent (
thm-reciprocity-fixed-exponent) and then to Kummer classes of Siegel units: how they
behave under diamond operators, a Mackey decomposition, and the congruence of their
In the second and third cases of the proof of thm-sha-bound, Ribet's method produces the
Selmer classes from irreducible lifts, with values in GSp_4, of reducible residual
representations built from χ and powers of the cyclotomic character.
thm-gsp4-lift-automorphy shows that these lifts are automorphic, which bounds the
Selmer groups. Its proof is a potential automorphy argument: the seeds (
thm-potential-automorphy-seeds) come from ordinary Hilbert modular forms with mixed
automorphy from rank two to rank four.

text.tspan: 5. The error term of the families

svg.text: This section shows where thm-sha-bound enters the estimates for families. Given a bound at
the primes 2 and 3, thm-family-sha-error-bound bounds the error term of the j-th
member of a family by eta_j ≤ d_j (C(fmbL^2 + Nlog^2 x) + sum_l log
lsum_(e<t)len Ш^1_l(E, e) ) (def-sha-error-term). The proof cuts each member
down to its good eigensystems and bounds the congruence valuation of each one prime by
prime: at the auxiliary primes g_0, g_1, at the primes q, d of the auxiliary pair, in an
intermediate range and at large primes. Each local bound combines the index theorem of
sec-sha-congruence with the lifting theorems of sec-sha-lifting.
thm-congruence-module-selmer-bound is the global index theorem behind the local
bounds of sec-sha-error: the length of the congruence module of an eigensystem π is at
most a sum of local lengths, a Selmer term, the lengths of Ш^1_l(E, e) and v_l(h_E). It is a
bound of the type of the numerical criterion of Wiles and Lenstra. Ribet's construction proves
it, turning congruences between π and other eigensystems into extensions of Galois
representations. def-congruence-data fixes the Hecke algebras and local data it needs.

text.tspan: 7. Local lifting theorems for crystalline lattices

svg.text: For a surjection T_1 → T_2 of crystalline lattices, the results here bound the cokernel of
H^1_f(T_1) → H^1_f(T_2) in terms of the Hodge–Tate weights; sec-sha-error uses them
to turn local lengths into Selmer lengths. thm-wach-lifting-theorem treats weights
clustered along the embeddings, through Wach modules. The other results treat clustered
windows (thm-lifting-clustered-weights, also with ramified coefficients), deep weights (
thm-lifting-potentially-crystalline, through the lattices of Bhatt and Scholze), and
describe the finite classes of cyclotomic twists (prop-finite-classes-cyclotomic-twists
